docs.title: Savoury — Hostel Mess Management System
docs.text:
Author(s):

  • 1024170252 Siddharth Singla
  • 1024170253 Vineet Tripathi
  • 1024170249 Shivansh Sahu

Savoury is a hostel mess (dining-hall) management platform. It provides a shared backend API with a student mobile app and an admin/staff web console for per-meal opt-in/opt-out booking, cutoff-driven locking, QR/roster-based attendance, and a wallet ledger with top-ups and semester-end cashouts.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
• code/backend-api — Express + TypeScript + Prisma (PostgreSQL) REST API shared by all clients.
  • code/mobile — Expo / React Native student app.
  • code/web — Vite + React admin / warden / staff console.

docs.title: Running the backend
docs.text:
cd code/backend-api
npm install
npx prisma generate
npm run dev

docs.title: Running the web console
docs.text:
cd code/web
npm install
npm run dev

docs.title: Running the mobile app
docs.text:
cd code/mobile
npm install
npx expo start

See the project proposal for the full requirements and design.

docs.title: Criteria for Project Selection
docs.text: This document defines the criteria we will use to choose projects for our software engineering course. It emphasizes time-to-value through rapid iterations, supported by CI/CD to enable frequent build, test, and delivery. Selection also considers contextual relevance, available engineering engines, scalability, and measurable evaluation criteria to ensure we build solutions that can be validated quickly and effectively.

docs.title: Time-to-value
docs.text: We shall design for rapid delivery, i.e. deliver meaningful increments within a short time window (say weekly). And, prioritize fast feedback over perfection, in order to reduce waiting time between decisions and results.
